# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Mar 20, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing L2 fork testing, improving conductor RPC functionality, and significant refactoring of CI acceptance tests to boost efficiency and reliability. Several critical issues related to dispute games and CI flakiness were also addressed.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Enhanced L2 Fork Testing Framework
A new L2 Fork Testing Framework has been added, significantly improving the ability to test L2 upgrades. This framework allows for generating upgrade bundles, forking L2 chains, executing bundles, and running tests via a `just` command wrapper around `forge`. This work addresses a key technical priority around developer tooling and documentation. ([#19464](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19464))

### Conductor RPC Improvements
The conductor RPC API now exposes the `DemoteVoter` method, enabling operators to demote a voting member to a non-voting member without requiring removal and re-addition of the node. This enhances the flexibility and operational efficiency of the consensus layer. ([#18700](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18700))

### CI Stability and Efficiency Enhancements
Significant efforts were made to improve the stability and efficiency of CI acceptance tests. This includes simplifying the acceptance CI process, removing flake-shake mechanisms, and parallelizing test runs. Additionally, a critical mutex deadlock in `VirtualNode.Start()` that caused tests to hang during shutdown was fixed, resolving a non-terminating CI job issue. Notifications for CI acceptance test failures were also updated to reflect proper ownership. ([#19679](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19679), [#19680](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19680), [#19684](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19684))

### Superauthority Payload Handling
The `op-node` now drops unsafe payloads denied by the Superauthority that lack a `DerivedFrom` value. This ensures that post-derived payloads explicitly denied by the Superauthority are not applied, enhancing protocol security. ([#19288](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19288))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- [#19689](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19689) fix(kona): fix action-tests-single CI job never running tests
- [#19688](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19688) fix(kona/genesis): continue past malformed logs in update_with_receipts
- [#19687](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19687) [NO-MERGE] fix(kona/derive): clear DAP on reset/activation signal in L1Retrieval
- [#19686](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19686) l1 retrieval: clear provider on reset
- [#19685](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19685) feat: opcm zk roots
- [#19683](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19683) fix(op-acceptance-tests): replace time.Sleep with deterministic block advancement in UnsafeChainNotStalling
- [#19682](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19682) fix(op-deployer): remove t.Parallel() from TestSuperchain to prevent CI flakes
- [#19678](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19678) fix(op-acceptance-tests): treat block removal as successful reorg detection

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Dispute Game Contract Refactoring and Cleanup
Several issues related to the dispute game contracts were closed, marking progress towards a more streamlined and efficient system. This includes refactoring proof contracts to support `Creator` contracts, stopping the deployment of blueprints for FDG and PDG, and the deletion of legacy dispute game contracts. The explicit game inputs handling for the `op-program` executor was also addressed, anticipating a future with only super games. ([#12421](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/12421), [#17262](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17262), [#17263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17263), [#15032](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/15032))

### L2 Fork Testing Infrastructure Established
The issue tracking the setup of L2 upgrade fork testing infrastructure has been closed, indicating the successful implementation of this critical testing capability. This infrastructure will enable more robust testing of L2 upgrades. ([#18837](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18837))

### CI Flakiness and Non-Terminating Jobs Resolved
A significant non-terminating CI job issue, specifically `memory-all-opn-op-geth`, was closed. This was attributed to a mutex deadlock in `VirtualNode.Start()` during shutdown, which has now been fixed. ([#19563](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19563))

### Kona + Cannon Fallback Proof Tracking
The issue tracking the work to ship Kona + Cannon as a fallback fault proof option has been closed, signifying progress in this area. ([#17237](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17237))

## NEW ISSUES

### Interop Phase 1: All Chains Use SuperDisputeGame
New issues have been opened to track the first phase of interoperability, where each chain independently upgrades to `SuperDisputeGame` on its own DGF, without shared infrastructure or invalid message support. This includes specific tasks for L1 Contracts, Supernode, Challenger/Proposer/Dispute-Mon, Kona Proof, Deployment Tooling, and other related components. ([#19690](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19690), [#19693](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19693), [#19694](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19694), [#19695](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19695), [#19696](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19696), [#19697](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19697), [#19698](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19698))

### Interop Phase 2: Merge Chains Into Shared Dispute Game
A series of issues have been created for the second phase of interoperability, focusing on merging chains into a shared `SuperDisputeGame` with shared DGF/ASR/ETHLockbox. This phase also includes message invalidation. Specific sub-issues cover L1 Contracts, L2 Contracts, Supernode, Message Invalidation, Deployment Tooling, and other aspects. ([#19691](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19691), [#19699](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19699), [#19700](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19700), [#19701](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19701), [#19702](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19702), [#19703](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19703), [#19704](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19704))

### Interop Phase 3: Removing Chains From Shared Dispute Games
Issues have been opened to address the ability to remove a chain from a shared dispute game, covering contracts, deployment tooling, and runbooks. ([#19692](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19692), [#19705](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19705), [#19706](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19706), [#19707](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19707))

### Flaky CI Tests
Two new flaky test reports were filed: `TestSupernodeInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` ([#19677](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19677)) and `TestCLELDivergence` ([#19681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19681)). These indicate intermittent failures in CI, with `TestCLELDivergence` potentially pointing to a real bug in the reset logic rather than just flakiness.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### op-reth: Recurring state root mismatch on Base mainnet causes permanent sync stall and fatal crash ([#19532](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19532))
The discussion on this issue continues, with a new comment suggesting a link to a specific `paradigmxyz/reth` issue. Previously, it was confirmed that custom chains like Manta Pacific are experiencing the same problem. A suggestion was made to open the issue at `base/base` if it's a general issue, and to ensure the latest OP Stack release is being used. The core problem remains recurring "mismatched block state root" errors
